successCriteria.description: leave.routes.ts instantiates LeaveService with all six constructor dependencies (leave-request repository, balance repository, employee repository, policy repository, audit service, unit of work) so the file type-checks against the current LeaveService constructor in src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts.

The approve, reject, and cancel handlers pass request.user.id as actorId and request.user.role as actorRole to the service methods, matching the ILeaveService signatures in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts; no client-supplied body field is used as the actor identity.
The apply handler passes request.user.id and request.user.role as the actor arguments to service.apply, so the audit record's performedBy reflects the authenticated caller rather than a body field.
A LeaveAuthorizationError raised by approve/reject/cancel is mapped to an HTTP 403 FORBIDDEN response (not a 500), so the manager-only authorization rule is observable at the API boundary.

constraints: The actor identity for every state-changing operation MUST come from request.user (populated by requireRole), never from a client-supplied body field such as approvedBy.

LeaveService must be constructed with all six dependencies declared by its constructor in src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts (leave-request repo, balance repo, employee repo, policy repo, audit service, unit of work).
No service-layer edit is in scope: the audit logging, balance deduction, and manager authorization logic already present in src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts must be preserved unchanged.
RBAC remains enforced by the route-level requireRole guard (GP-005); the handler must not re-implement role checks inline.
outOfScope: Editing src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts — the audit logging, balance deduction, and manager authorization logic are already implemented and must remain unchanged.
Registering leave routes in src/app.ts — route registration is not part of the three gate findings and is deferred.
Restoring deducted balance when an APPROVED request is cancelled — not one of the three findings and not required by this phase.

ambiguities.description: Should leave routes be registered in src/app.ts? Currently only uptimeRoutes is registered, so the leave endpoints are unreachable even after the routes file is fixed.
options: Register leaveRoutes in app.ts as part of this phase

entityInvariants.invariant: approvedBy is always derived from the authenticated actor (request.user.id), never from a client-supplied body field; it is null until an approve/reject transition stamps it.
Lifecycle transitions remain PENDING → APPROVED | REJECTED and PENDING | APPROVED → CANCELLED; any other transition throws InvalidLeaveRequestTransitionError (unchanged by this phase).
Approving a request deducts its inclusive day count from usedDays/remainingDays atomically with the status change and audit record (already implemented in the service; this phase must not break it).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: MANAGER or HR_ADMIN; the actor must be the employee's manager (Employee.managerId) unless HR_ADMIN, enforced by the service's authorization check.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveAuthorizationError → 403 FORBIDDEN; InvalidLeaveRequestTransitionError/InsufficientLeaveBalanceError/OverlappingLeaveError → 400 CONFLICT; missing request → 404 NOT_FOUND.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The route handlers must call the service methods with the exact signatures declared by ILeaveService (apply(input, actorId, actorRole); approve/reject/cancel(id, actorId, actorRole)) — no positional mismatch or omitted actor arguments.
The LeaveService constructor invocation must supply the six dependencies in the order declared by the class constructor (leaveRequests, balances, employees, policies, audit, uow).
The actor identity must be read from request.user (id and role), whose shape is declared by the AuthenticatedUser augmentation and populated by requireRole.

Error responses must conform to the standard shape { error: string; code: string } with the codes VALIDATION_ERROR / UNAUTHORIZED / FORBIDDEN / NOT_FOUND / CONFLICT as established by the reconciled error contract.
